ours-errorbars.short: Night School's error-bar measurements, computed for this film
ours-errorbars.citation: media/school/errorbars/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_errorbars.mjs from system/school/errorbars.mjs and errorbars-truth.mjs: the attention model scored on 1,024 held-out rows; percentile and normal bootstrap intervals by row and by word at 16, 64, 256 and 1,024 rows; the generator's exact expected loss and 1,000-trial coverage checks; a duplicated-row control; a paired comparison of two S17 students; five seeds per student.
claims: Loss 0.6676 and accuracy 0.7332 on 1,024 rows; row-bootstrap widths 0.0838, 0.0559, 0.0311, 0.0161 at 16, 64, 256, 1,024 rows.
Exact truth 0.6361; row percentile coverage 0.934, 0.931, 0.953 at 16, 64, 256 rows; word-level 0.998 to 1; 16 rows copied four times 0.669, by distinct row 0.933.
Paired difference -0.0045 [-0.0081, -0.0011], unpaired 3.27 times as wide; seed spread 11.8 times the row standard error.
ours-errorbars.n: 1,024 rows; 1,000 coverage trials per size; 5 seeds per student.
ours-errorbars.does_not_prove: Anything about large models or other test sets; the rows here are balanced by position, which is why word-level intervals came out too wide.

efron1979.short: Efron 1979, Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife
efron1979.citation: Efron, B. (1979). Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife. The Annals of Statistics 7(1), 1-26.
efron1979.read: to be read by the fact-check
claims: Introduces the bootstrap: estimate the sampling distribution of a statistic by resampling the observed data with replacement.

miller2024.short: Miller 2024, Adding Error Bars to Evals
miller2024.citation: Miller, E. (2024). Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations. arXiv:2411.00640.
miller2024.read: to be read by the fact-check
claims: Evaluation questions that come in related groups need clustered standard errors, which can be much larger than the naive ones; paired differences reduce variance when two models answer the same questions.
